title: Contain kernel selection stochasticity: experimentation and remediation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
During a capacity surge on 2026-02-08 we observed repeated p95 latency regressions across mid- and long-context generation workloads. Root-cause analysis points to amplified stochasticity in the kernel selection scoring pipeline combined with scheduler probe amplification and an attention autotile toggle that occasionally flips during warmups. The result was kernel churn (frequent changes of execution path for the same request shape) and KV-cache warmup misses, which increased tail latency and unit cost.

Key symptoms observed:
- p95 for text-generation endpoints rose from baseline ~120ms to ~420ms for 1k token sessions during the incident window.
- Kernel-selection entropy metric (sampled across workers) increased ~6x concurrently with surge onset.
- Autoscaler probe rate increased modestly; scheduler heuristics reacted by probing candidate kernels more often, which amplified selection noise.
- Attention autotile retriggered after certain microbatch interactions, causing temporary dequant path selection and KV warmup loss.

Repro steps (synthetic):
1) Run synthetic arrival pattern with 40% long-context (>= 512 tokens) concurrently with a background of short bursts (<= 64 tokens) for 30 minutes.
2) Use bench harness: python bench/run_surge.py --concurrency=480 --long_frac=0.4 --pattern=zipf --duration=1800 --seed=202602
3) Collect kernel_assignment_hist, kv_cache_miss_rate, and p95 traces.

Hypothesis (root cause):
The kernel scoring model combines noisy micro-metrics (sampled latency, memory pressure, microbatch acceptance) with a freshness term. Under surge, sampling variance and scheduler probe amplification increased the freshness term's influence, making the scoring unstable. This combined with an attention autotile probe that occasionally flips execution path triggered cache invalidations and dequant fallbacks. Net effect: high kernel churn and transient performance regressions.

Short-term mitigations already deployed (observed improvement):
- Temporarily disabled non-essential kernel probing during autoscaler bursts (hotfix 1289). Observed p95 reduction ~35% in internal canary within 1 hour.
- Raised hysteresis for attention autotile flip to require 3 consecutive microbatches of consistent shape before toggling. Reduced autotile flips by ~70% in synthetic tests.

Proposed long-term plan (this ticket covers experimentation + remediation):
1) Quantify stochasticity and create a stable metric: kernel_assignment_entropy (owner: Jonah Kim, due: 2026-02-20). Add to runtime dashboards and incident alerting.
2) Experiment: anneal freshness weighting and add a dampening term to kernel score to reduce rapid switches. Controlled A/B experiment funnel (owners: Jonah Kim, Priya Nair). Steps:
   - Implement parameterized damping_factor (0.0-1.0) + exponential decay of freshness influence.
   - Run grid of damping_factor=[0.1,0.25,0.5] on synthetic surge and measure p95, throughput, and unit cost.
   - Choose default that reduces churn without increasing baseline latency >5%.
   (ETA for first results: 2 weeks)
3) Scheduler: introduce probe-rate cap and entropy-aware backoff. When kernel_assignment_entropy > threshold, the scheduler should back off probing and favor the incumbent kernel. (owner: Daniel Berg, due: 2026-03-03)
4) Attention autotile: formalize a guarded state machine with explicit warmup windows and cache-safe toggles. Require KV-cache checkpoint alignment before any path flip. (owner: Maria Lopez, due: 2026-03-10)
5) Canary and rollout plan: three-phase rollout after experiments pass QA:
   - Internal canary (0.5% traffic) for 24h, monitor p95, kernel_entropy, kv_cache_miss; automatic rollback on >20% p95 regression.
   - Cross-region canary (10% traffic) 48h, monitor same metrics plus customer-facing error rates.
   - Gradual ramp 10->25->50->100% over 4 days with safety gates.
6) Runbook updates: add steps to throttle probing and to manually pin kernel version per route during incidents. (owner: SRE team, due: 2026-03-05)

Metrics and monitoring (examples to add to dashboards/alerts):
- kernel_assignment_entropy: sum(rate(kernel_assignment_entropy_sample[1m])) by (worker)
- kv_cache_miss_rate: rate(kv_cache_miss_total[5m]) / rate(kv_cache_access_total[5m])
- p95_generation_latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(generation_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le))
Alert thresholds suggested:
- kernel_assignment_entropy > 3x baseline for 5m -> P1 paging
- kv_cache_miss_rate > 0.05 for 10m -> Investigate autotile toggles

Acceptance criteria for merge to main:
- A/B experiment shows >=30% reduction in kernel churn with <=5% change in baseline p50 latency and no increased error rate.
- Runbook updated and on-call trained on new throttle knobs.
- Automated canary with rollback triggers implemented.

Rollforward / rollback plan:
- Rollforward incremental via feature-flag. If canary triggers, auto-rollback to previous flag state and open ENG rollback issue.

Open questions / tradeoffs considered:
- Aggressive damping may reduce opportunities for better kernels under legitimate hardware/resource change. We will limit damping to short windows and allow manual overrides per-customer workload.
- Probe-rate caps reduce exploration; need to ensure new kernels with genuine better performance still get discovered. We'll add periodic low-rate background sweeping to keep discovery alive.

Artifacts and reproducible assets:
- bench notebook: drive://redwood/runtime/benchmarks/kernel-stoch-notebook.ipynb
- PR with hotfix and experiment branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1289 (hotfix), https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1297 (experiment)
- Incident writeup: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runtime/postmortems/kernel-stochasticity-2026-02

Next steps this sprint (concrete):
- Jonah: implement kernel_assignment_entropy metric and dashboard (due 2026-02-20).
- Daniel: implement probe-rate cap and entropy backoff in scheduler (due 2026-03-03).
- Maria: finalize autotile state machine and KV-safe flip (due 2026-03-10).
- SRE: prepare canary jobs and rollback automation (due 2026-03-12).
- PM (Priya): coordinate QA, customer communication template, and set release window (milestone runtime-2.4).

If anything blocks progress (access to bench infra, long synthetic run cost), note here and we will escalate to Eng leadership.
